sentences.text: The only known species in this newly proposed genus is Rexarthuria cliftii.
Fossil remains were found in the upper Tunbridge Wells Sand Formation in England, and the specific name honors William Clift, curator of the Hunterian Museum.
Rexarthuria is a new combination because the species was originally placed in the genus Palaeornis, a name that was preoccupied by a bird.
This animal lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Valanginian age, at the type locality of the Tunbridge Wells Sand Formation.

Scientific opinions on its placement vary; Witton and colleagues classified it as a lonchodectid in 2009, Thomas and McDavid analyzed it as a sister group to Tapejaridae in 2025, and Averianov referred it to indeterminate Azhdarchoidea in 2012 and 2014.
